quote.text: When people injure you, ask yourself what good or harm they thought would come of it. If you understand that, you'll feel sympathy rather than outrage or anger. Your sense of good and evil may be the same as theirs, or near it, in which case you have to excuse them. Or your sense of good and evil may differ from theirs. In which case they're misguided and deserve your compassion. Is that so hard?
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • When a child’s misbehavior arises, pause to consider the lessons behind it; often, their actions stem from inexperience or unmet needs, not malice.
    • Embrace compassion over anger—by understanding a child's perspective, you nurture growth, teaching them empathy and self-awareness.
  • Leadership:
    • In leadership, remember that even when colleagues or subordinates act in ways that seem harmful, their intent is often rooted in differing values or misunderstandings.
    • By striving to understand and empathize with their motivations, you cultivate a culture of mutual respect and open dialogue, fostering a unified team.
  • Product Management:
    • When feedback or resistance challenges your vision, reflect on the intent behind it; stakeholders might be driven by genuine concerns or misinterpretations rather than ill will.
    • Transform perceived obstacles into opportunities for insightful dialogue—a compassionate approach can refine product strategies and bridge gaps in expectations.
